Huang *''Skimmia orthoclada'' Hayata *''Skimmia reevesiana'' (Fortune) Fortune }} |synonyms_ref = {{citation |url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-2860579 |title=The Plant List: A Working List of All Plant Species |access-date=8 December 2016}} }} {{Infobox Chinese |title=''Ilex cornuta'' |c=枸骨 |p=gǒugǔ |y=gáu-gwāt }} '''''Ilex cornuta''''', commonly known as '''Chinese holly'''{{PLANTS|id=ILCO80|taxon=Ilex cornuta|accessdate=22 January 2016}} or '''horned holly''',{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }} is a slow-growing, densely foliaged evergreen shrub in the [[Aquifoliaceae]] plant family. It is native to eastern [[China]] and [[Korea]]Hillier Nurseries, The Hillier Manual of Trees and Shrubs, David & Charles, 1998, p281 and attains a height of about {{convert|3|metres|ft}}. The leaves are usually 5-spined (sometimes 4), between 3.5 cm and 10 cm long,Phillips, R. & Rix, M., Shrubs, Macmillan, 1994, p277 oblong and [[Leaf shape|entire]]. The fruits are red berries, which are larger than those of the European Holly (''[[Ilex aquifolium]]''). ''Ilex cornuta'' is valued horticulturally for its attractive and distinctive rectangular foliage and for its large red berries. Several [[cultivar]]s and hybrids have been introduced by the horticultural trade, including 'Burfordii' (compact and free-fruiting), 'Dazzler' (large fruits), 'Dwarf Burfordii' (particularly compact), and 'Nellie R. Stevens' (a hybrid with ''I. aquifolium'', very free-fruiting). ''Ilex cornuta'' and its cultivars will tolerate a wide variety of soils and will grow in sun or shade. == Description == ''Ilex cornuta'' is a broadleaf evergreen shrub that can grow up to 2.5 metres (8 ft) tall. It has been recorded as growing up to 7.6 metres (25 ft) tall. Leaves are rectangular that have 4 to 5 spines on the leaf margin. The glossy and leathery leaves are simple and alternate on the stem.{{Cite web|title=Ilex cornuta (Chinese Holly, Horned Holly) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/ilex-cornuta/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}} Flowers begin to bloom during the early spring and are a dull white color and have a fragrance. The flowers produce red berries that ripen in early fall.{{Cite web|title=Ilex cornuta - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276168&isprofile=0&#:~:text=It%20is%20a%20broadleaf%20evergreen,are%20fragrant%20but%20generally%20inconspicuous.|access-date=2020-11-19|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}} The bark is a light gray color and smooth. As it grows, the bark turns into a finely flaky appearance. The stem of ''Ilex cornuta'' is either green or a red to burgundy color depending on the season. The green stems turn slightly more red during the winter months. ''Ilex cornuta'' is dioecious, meaning the flowers found on the shrub are either female or male. Male and female flowers are not found together on the same plant, so the plant is not self-fertile, it takes a male and a female plant to reproduce.{{Cite web|title=Ilex cornuta Horned Holly, Chinese holly PFAF Plant Database|url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Ilex+cornuta|access-date=2020-11-19|website=pfaf.org}} == Distribution and habitat == ''Ilex cornuta'' is native to the central and southeastern parts of China, Hainan, and Korea. ''Ilex cornuta'' was introduced to the United States and is currently considered invasive.{{Cite web|title=Ilex cornuta Lindl. & Paxton {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:83182-1|access-date=2020-10-14|website=Plants of the World Online|language=en}} It has been observed naturalized in the eastern United States, found most prominently in North Carolina, Alabama, and Kentucky.{{Cite web|title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0|url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.156812/Ilex_cornuta|access-date=2020-10-14|website=explorer.natureserve.org}} ''Ilex cornuta'' is tolerant of most soils except those that are poorly drained. It can be grown in partial and full sun and is tolerant of the heat and humidity.{{Cite web|title=Ilex cornuta (Chinese Holly, Horned Holly) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/ilex-cornuta/|access-date=2020-11-04|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}} The shrub can be found between 150 and 600 meters elevation and along mountain ridges that have full sun.{{Cite web|title=Ilex cornuta Horned Holly, Chinese holly PFAF Plant Database|url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Ilex+cornuta|access-date=2020-11-04|website=pfaf.org}} == Landscape uses== ''Ilex cornuta'' is used for winter interest and drought tolerant gardens, as barriers, for privacy, and hedges. The Chinese holly can attract bees, other pollinators, songbirds, and specialized bees. The biggest problem with Chinese holly in the landscape are its spines. == Conservation status == According to the IUCN red list, the ''Ilex cornuta'' is of least concern. Its population trend is considered stable during the last assessment in 2018.{{Cite journal|date=2018-12-06|last1=Ye|first1=J|last2=Qin|first2=H.N.|last3=Oldfield|first3=S|title=Ilex cornuta|journal=The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species|url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/18776178/84008871|language=en}} == References == {{Commons}} {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q1074050}} [[Category:Ilex|cornuta]] [[Category:Trees of Asia]] [[Category:Trees of China]] [[Category:Trees of Korea]] [[Category:Flora of Asia]]
